nodes.label: Device-code sign-in and token cache
nodes.rationale: Refresh token cached in .token_cache.json so later runs never prompt and are safe to schedule.

nodes.label: Exit code 1 on expired sign-in or unreadable mailbox
nodes.norm_label: exit code 1 on expired sign-in or unreadable mailbox
nodes.rationale: Lets a scheduler flag the failure while run still carries on with already-stored alerts.

nodes.label: Enrichment
nodes.rationale: Personal-scale only: capped, delayed, cached, and stops when LinkedIn blocks (429/999) to stay polite.

nodes.label: Job store
nodes.rationale: Single owner of all persisted Alerts and Job knowledge; answers which Jobs need details or a score.

nodes.label: Prompt hash
nodes.rationale: Fingerprinting model + effort + instructions + CV + Rubric + schema makes scoring incremental: only unscored or stale jobs are re-sent to Claude.

nodes.label: Rubric
nodes.rationale: The candidate's own priorities override the model's general opinion.

nodes.label: Batch API scoring (--batch, resume)
nodes.rationale: 50% cheaper and asynchronous; Ctrl+C while waiting is safe and resume collects the batch later.

nodes.label: Data and privacy (git-ignored data/ contents)
nodes.rationale: Alert emails carry LinkedIn auth tokens and the token cache acts like a password, so only data/rubric.md is tracked.

nodes.norm_label: inbox read split: job store writes emails/, reads via folder adapter
nodes.rationale: Kept on purpose: it has caused no bugs, and giving the Job store sole ownership would require importing samples through fetch, delaying dropped-in samples until the next fetch/run. Rejected options: Job store reads emails/ itself (still depends on Alert source, nothing gained); samples become an Alert source that fetch imports (delays samples, import must keep working when Outlook sign-in fails).
